n: The platypus is a mammal native to eastern Australia.
Unlike most mammals, it lays eggs.
It uses its bill to detect electric fields produced by prey underwater.
Its young feed on milk produced by the mother.
goal: emphasize a way in which the platypus differs from most mammals
c: Unlike most mammals, the platypus lays eggs.
The platypus, a mammal, is native to eastern Australia.
Platypus young feed on milk produced by their mother.
The platypus hunts for prey underwater.
x: The goal is a difference from most mammals. Only this choice states one directly.
t: Feeding young on milk is something most mammals do, so it’s a similarity.

n: Mary Anning (1799–1847) was a fossil collector in Lyme Regis, England.
As a young girl, she helped uncover one of the first ichthyosaur skeletons to be scientifically identified.
She later found one of the first plesiosaur skeletons.
Because she was a woman, she was excluded from the Geological Society of London.
goal: present Anning’s discoveries to an audience unfamiliar with her
c: Anning was excluded from the Geological Society of London because she was a woman.
Mary Anning, a nineteenth-century fossil collector from Lyme Regis, England, found early ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons.
One of the first ichthyosaur skeletons was uncovered with the help of a young girl.
Lyme Regis, England, was home to Mary Anning from 1799 to 1847.
x: An unfamiliar audience needs to know who she was and what she found. Only this choice does both.
t: The first choice is about her exclusion, not her discoveries.

n: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor.
They support about 25% of all marine species.
Rising ocean temperatures can cause corals to expel the algae living in their tissues, a process called bleaching.
Bleached corals can recover if temperatures return to normal quickly.
goal: emphasize how important coral reefs are relative to their size
c: Although coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor, they support about 25% of all marine species.
Rising ocean temperatures can cause corals to bleach.
Bleached corals can recover if temperatures return to normal quickly.
Coral reefs, which can bleach, support many marine species.
x: “Relative to their size” needs both numbers: tiny area, huge share of species.
t: The last choice mentions species but leaves out the size comparison.

n: The Harlem Renaissance was a cultural movement centered in New York City’s Harlem neighborhood.
It flourished in the 1920s and early 1930s.
Langston Hughes wrote poetry that drew on the rhythms of jazz and blues.
Zora Neale Hurston wrote novels and collected folklore in the American South.
goal: make a generalization about the kinds of work produced during the Harlem Renaissance
c: Langston Hughes wrote poetry that drew on the rhythms of jazz and blues.
The Harlem Renaissance flourished in the 1920s and early 1930s.
Writers of the Harlem Renaissance produced varied work, from jazz-influenced poetry to novels and collections of folklore.
Zora Neale Hurston collected folklore in the American South.
x: A generalization covers the range of work. Only this choice sums up several kinds together.
t: The first and last choices are single examples, not generalizations.

n: Tardigrades are microscopic animals about 0.5 millimeters long.
They can survive temperatures from near absolute zero to above 150°C.
They have survived short periods in the vacuum of space.
In harsh conditions, they dry out and enter a state called cryptobiosis.
goal: explain how tardigrades survive harsh conditions
c: Tardigrades are microscopic animals about 0.5 millimeters long.
In harsh conditions, tardigrades dry out and enter a state called cryptobiosis.
Tardigrades have been studied by scientists for many years.
Tardigrades are about 0.5 millimeters long and live in many places.
x: The goal is how they survive. Cryptobiosis is the mechanism.
t: Their size doesn’t explain how they survive.

n: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mold had contaminated one of his bacteria cultures.
The bacteria near the mold had been killed.
The mold was later identified as a species of Penicillium.
Penicillin, the substance produced by the mold, became one of the first widely used antibiotics.
goal: explain the significance of Fleming’s observation
c: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed mold in one of his bacteria cultures.
Fleming’s observation that mold had killed bacteria led to penicillin, one of the first widely used antibiotics.
The mold Fleming observed was later identified as a species of Penicillium.
Bacteria near the mold in Fleming’s culture had been killed.
x: Significance means why it mattered: it led to one of the first widely used antibiotics.
t: The first choice describes the observation but not why it mattered.

n: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
Some of its weather stations have never recorded rain.
Its dry, clear skies make it an excellent location for astronomical observatories.
Several major telescopes have been built there.
goal: explain why astronomers build telescopes in the Atacama Desert
c: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
Some weather stations in the Atacama Desert have never recorded rain.
Because of its dry, clear skies, the Atacama Desert is an excellent place for astronomical observatories.
Several major telescopes have been built in Chile.
x: “Why” calls for a reason. The clear skies are the reason.
t: Dryness alone doesn’t mention astronomy at all.

n: Alligators have broad, U-shaped snouts.
Crocodiles have narrower, V-shaped snouts.
Alligators live mainly in freshwater habitats.
Many crocodile species can tolerate salt water.
goal: contrast alligators and crocodiles in terms of habitat
c: Alligators have U-shaped snouts, while crocodiles have V-shaped snouts.
Alligators live mainly in freshwater habitats, whereas many crocodile species can tolerate salt water.
Alligators and crocodiles are both reptiles with distinctive snouts.
Many crocodile species can tolerate salt water.
x: The goal names both a contrast and a topic (habitat). Only this choice does both.
t: The first choice contrasts them, but by snout shape instead of habitat.

n: Maria Tallchief (1925–2013) was an American ballerina.
She was a member of the Osage Nation.
She is often called America’s first major prima ballerina.
She danced with the New York City Ballet from 1948 to 1965.
goal: introduce Maria Tallchief and her significance
c: Maria Tallchief, a member of the Osage Nation, is often called America’s first major prima ballerina.
Maria Tallchief danced with the New York City Ballet from 1948 to 1965.
Maria Tallchief lived from 1925 to 2013.
The New York City Ballet employed many dancers between 1948 and 1965.
x: An introduction says who she was. “First major prima ballerina” says why she matters.
t: The dates are facts about her, but they don’t show her significance.

n: A study tested two groups of students on vocabulary.
Group 1 studied the words by rereading a list.
Group 2 studied the same words by quizzing themselves.
A week later, Group 2 remembered 50% more words than Group 1.
c: In the study, students who quizzed themselves remembered 50% more words a week later than students who reread a list.
The study tested two groups of students on vocabulary.
Group 1 studied by rereading a list, and Group 2 studied the same words.
Rereading a list is one way students study vocabulary.
x: A conclusion states the result: self-quizzing beat rereading. (That’s also why this game quizzes you.)
t: The second choice describes the setup, not the result.
